podcast.body: This song, originally a jingle for Crocker Citizens Bank, was famously transformed into a hit by The Carpenters. Richard Carpenter heard the ad and was convinced of its potential, with Karen Carpenter's vocals bringing it to life. It reached number 2 on the Hot 100 in November 1970, becoming an instant soft rock classic and is regarded as their signature hit. "Number 2 was as high as the Carpenter's version got on the Hot 100."

podcast.body: This song, released in late 1970, started as a failed jingle for the Crocker National Bank of California, part of a campaign designed by Hal Reiner and Partners to appeal to young couples. Songwriter Paul Williams, struggling at the time, was tasked with writing the jingle, which initially had only two verses and a bridge. Richard Carpenter saw the TV commercial, got excited, and tracked Williams down, leading to a finished version of the song. It sold a million copies, spent seven weeks at number one, ten weeks in the top ten, and earned the Carpenters two Grammy Awards. "This song, this giant hit, this multi-million dollar success started as a failed jingle in a bank commercial."
